title: linux / Configure {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} as the default text editor
content:
## Configure {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} as the default text editor

### xdg-open

Set {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} as the default text editor for text files, `text/plain`, used by `xdg-open`:

```bash
xdg-mime default code.desktop text/plain
```

### Debian alternatives system

Debian-based distributions support setting a default **editor** through the [Debian alternatives system](https://wiki.debian.org/DebianAlternatives), without concern for the MIME type. Set {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} as the default editor with this command:

```bash
sudo update-alternatives --set editor /usr/bin/code
```

If {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} was installed with the Snap package, use this command instead:

```bash
sudo update-alternatives --set editor /snap/bin/code
```

If {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} doesn't show up as an alternative to the default `editor`, register it:

```bash
sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/editor editor $(which code) 10
```
